creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A pane whose bridge has ended and whose replacement never started cannot get another one for the life of the app process. Its agent is alive, its terminal is free, the daemon answers - and the only recovery is quitting Muster and opening it again. Two Claude Code sessions were unreachable for 90 minutes today, each holding an unsent prompt.

## Why it cannot recover

A surface is rebuilt on exactly two conditions (`PaneSurfaces.borrow`): its control socket moved, or its `bridgeRestarts` count moved. Only a new surface can start a bridge, because a bridge is the surface's command.

`bridgeRestarts` advances only in `Respawns::ended` (`crates/muster-core/src/respawn.rs:176`), which is called when a bridge ends. With no bridge running, nothing ends, so nothing advances the count, so no surface is built, so no bridge runs. The control socket is `/private/tmp/muster-<app pid>-<daemon>.sock` and is fixed for the life of the process, so the other condition cannot fire either.

Neither of the two ways out helps. `muster pane close` sends `ClosePane` to the daemon and ends the pane, which kills the agent this is trying to reach. And the CLI has no verb that asks for a bridge: `muster pane` offers new, rename, send, read, close, move, resize.

## What was measured

Run 34598, 0.6.0, herdr 0.8.0, 2026-09-04. The devenv box was starved by an unrelated runaway process (load average 185), which broke every bridge. Eight panes recovered. Two did not:

    18:13:15.459  bridge:w4:p1  bridge.closed        herdr's stream ended without a closing frame
    18:13:15.459  bridge:w4:p1  bridge.attach.failed herdr's stream ended without a closing frame
    18:13:15.460  app           bridge.ended
    18:13:15.947  app           bridge.replacing     pane=devenv/p206y9p61r attempt=1
    (nothing further for this pane; the log runs to 18:32)

The core decided to replace and said so. No `bridge.start` followed, and `ps` showed no bridge process for either pane. `bridge.replacing.stopped` never appears in the log, so this is not the respawn ladder giving up at `LIMIT` - the ladder was still willing. The replacement was decided and never began, and that leaves the pane in the state above with nothing able to move it.

Everything else was healthy while the panes stayed dead. Measured at 18:35, twenty minutes after the box recovered:

    herdr pane list over Muster's own forwarded socket:  0.26 s, all four panes listed
    ssh -O check on Muster's master:                     master running
    echo through Muster's ssh master:                    0.45 s
    herdr clients holding w4:p1 or w4:pC:                none
    muster pane read on the dead panes:                  answered, agent screens intact

So the daemon, the transport and the terminals were all fine. Only the window could not get back to them.

## What it cost

Two agents in `~/src/notes/chicago`, both idle with a prompt typed and unsent: `push all of this` at 46% context, and `draft the message to chris on cash-only and v+1` at 48%. Recovery took quitting the app, ending an orphaned ssh master with `ssh -O exit`, killing the two herdr clients left holding terminals, deleting stale sockets, and relaunching. All four panes then came back with their agents and their unsent prompts.

## Fix

Give a pane with no bridge a way to get one.

1. **A verb.** `muster pane reattach --pane X`: ask the daemon whether the pane exists, and if it does, advance `bridgeRestarts` so the shell builds a surface. This is the whole fix for a person who can see the pane is dead, and it is what the run log should name instead of the advice it gives now.
2. **Notice without being asked.** The typeable watch already reports a pane nothing is dialing five seconds after its bridge exits (`respawn.rs:240-242`). That watch knows the exact condition. A pane in it whose daemon still lists the pane should get a bridge, or offer one through `a_2Inq5D1VZ`.
3. **Find out why the replacement never started.** The core published a decision the shell did not act on. Worth knowing whether a parked pane, a hidden tab, or a spawn that failed under load is the reason, because a decision that silently does nothing is the part that turned a broken connection into a dead pane.

## Two smaller things found beside it

- **The remedy in the give-up message destroys what it recovers.** `respawn::gave_up` ends with "Closing this pane and opening it again starts a fresh bridge", but closing a pane ends its agent. For a pane whose agent is alive - which is the ordinary case, since the daemon holds the PTY and only the connection died - that advice costs the user the session. The sentence should say to reattach, once there is something to name.
- **A first bridge cannot take a terminal back.** `bridgeRestarts` is zero on a fresh launch, so the first bridge never passes `--takeover` (`PaneTree.swift:217-220`). A herdr client left holding a terminal by the previous app therefore refuses the new window's attach, and nothing in the window says so. This recovery needed the clients killed by hand on the far machine first. A relaunch that adopts panes it finds in its own saved state is not a first bridge in the sense that rule is protecting, and could say so.
title: 🔌 A pane whose bridge never restarted is dead until Muster is relaunched, agent and all
